name: Lele Pons
scope: Dedicated Lele audit. Only this report and tests/character-audits/lele.test.ts were written in the repository; no runtime edits, commits, additional server or child agents.

identityAndPortrayal.preservedDossier: The preserved dossier identifies the Caracas-born creator, comedian and singer and explicitly describes the fighting actions as fiction. No new broad web research was required.
identityAndPortrayal.visualMatch: Actual sprites preserve long blonde waves with darker roots, yellow hoodie, blue jeans, pale sneakers and a pink phone. Hair, face, clothes and phone remain coherent between the eight combat poses and both facings. The small cheek mole could not be reliably judged at the inspected screen size.
identityAndPortrayal.adaptation: Phone salute, Camera-ready/viral/prank combo names and a delayed ground peel fit the established humor-and-content adaptation. Existing likeness and clothing were preserved.
identityAndPortrayal.audio: The dossier specifies generic wordless effort/pain reactions and a prank special cue. Audio playback was not audited and no dialogue was introduced.

movementAndStance.jump: First jump reaches y454.6 after ten calls; second jump is accepted and third jump rejected. Landing restores y554, grounded=true, jumps=0, with both stocks retained.
movementAndStance.sprites: Production drawSprite showed all eight frames in both facings: phone idle0, guard1, movement2/3, tucked jump4, punch5, high kick6, recoil7. No head, hand, shoe or silhouette clipping and no detached neighboring fragment were observed.

cpuFight.method: Real shared-engine match after full intro; Lele idles180 calls to allow CPU offense, then chases and uses guard/jump/light/heavy/special/super actions. Entire bout runs twice and full final state matches exactly.
cpuFight.limitation: Heavy starts but does not land in this deterministic bout; targeted tests verify its damage and guard behavior. This is an exercised complete fight, not a balance benchmark.

introAndSelection.name: Saludo a la cámara
introAndSelection.method: Own native T3 tab opened with reuseExistingTab=false and explicitly targeted throughout. Production loadSprite/drawSprite/drawPresentation/renderMatch imported directly into ephemeral browser canvases. No repository visual harness written.
introAndSelection.observations: All eight combat poses drawn right/left. Intro and selection sampled at progress0,.25,.5,.75,1 in both facings. Phone pose and small camera/sparkle accents transition back to guard frame1; no duplicated phone was observed. Actual split-screen cinematic rendered at tick72 with Lele P1 and tick252 with Lele P2, facing the rival correctly in each slot. Actual fight snapshots show moving peel at10, planted peel at27 and impact at36.
introAndSelection.oneShot: selectionProgress clamps to1 at2800ms and remains1 at5600ms. Portrait.tsx requests animation frames only while progress<1. Start/end intro and selection poses return to frame1. Real-engine intro consumes attempted special and holds position for509 ticks, then begins playing at510, on both sides.
introAndSelection.transientInterruption: A shared-dev-server reload removed the first ephemeral canvas; attempting to reuse it produced TypeError reading getContext of null. Console logged a504 Outdated Request and ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. Recreating the canvas in the same owned tab restored renderer checks. No alternate browser or server was started.
introAndSelection.limitations: Representative deterministic samples were inspected, not every interpolation frame or audio synchronization. The tab was closed successfully through t3_preview_close.

recommendation: Retain Lele's current behavior and visual presentation; this focused audit reproduced no Lele-specific runtime defect.
